card.band: 8 h. There are several levers (prefilter, traversal, contention), so partial credit is steady. A frontier agent gets one or two of them. A weaker model breaks output order or correctness.
card.cheat: Calling a newer regex crate is not possible because the vendored copy is pinned and the build is offline. Output-gated differential tests catch dropped matches.
card.grading: The correctness gate is the existing test suite plus generated pattern/corpus differential output against the sealed 13.0.0 binary (set-equal results and match text). Wall-clock medians on hidden corpora. Reward 2^u - 1 against the reference.
card.reference: ripgrep 14.0.0 (speedups not published, measured by us on the same corpora). Overlap with the existing regex speedup card is noted: the traversal and prefilter levers are the new ones.
card.task: /app ships a history-less snapshot of ripgrep 13.0.0 with its vendored crates and a benchmark harness over large trees. Agent speeds up searches with word-boundary and look-around patterns, the literal prefilter, and parallel directory traversal.
card.title: ripgrep 13 to 14 look-around prefilter and traversal speedup

source_notes: q:"Make most searches with `\b` look-arounds (among others) much faster." Levers: inner-literal prefilter (#1746), look-around handling (#1760), work-stealing parallel directory traversal (#2591), reduced contention (#2642). 13.0.0: vectorised memmem, stat-call ordering. Multi-lever incl. parallelism and I/O. Speedups would need own measurement: INFERRED, not on page. 14.0.0 also depends on regex 1.9 rewrite (overlap with regex rows).

full_card.band: 8 h tier. Several levers (prefilter, traversal, contention, look-around). Frontier likely gets 1-2 levers; weaker model breaks output order or correctness. No dated public evidence: E0.

Build.why: Offline vendoring of 13.0.0 crates, harness and corpora: about 3-5 days.

Fit.why: CPU and memory fit; parallel wall-clock timings may be noisy under gVisor.

Hor.why: 8 h with several levers and a benchmark harness over large trees.

Lic.why: Unlicense OR MIT, both files present in 13.0.0.

Multi.why: Four levers (prefilter, look-around, traversal, contention) give steady partial credit.

Nov.why: Same-subject neighbours at cosine 0.22-0.32 and overlap with the regex speedup card on \b look-arounds.

Ref.why: 14.0.0 is a complete permissive reference, but its \b gain is partly from the regex rewrite the agent cannot reach; S needs our own measurement.

spike_plan.kill_if: Traversal-only gain under 1.05x and essentially all of the gain comes from the regex rewrite (reference not reachable by the agent); or run-to-run noise above about 25% so wall-clock medians cannot be graded.
spike_plan.pass_if: 14.0.0 is at least 1.3x faster than 13.0.0 on the traversal-only run and at least 1.5x on the \b or look-around runs; outputs are set-equal; IQR under about 15% across 5 runs.
steps: In a throwaway networked Linux container, fetch the 13.0.0 and 14.0.0 tags, run cargo vendor for each, and build both release binaries offline (smoke_build was skipped, so this build is the first evidence).
Build a synthetic corpus of about 100k files with mixed sizes, plus a large real tree (e.g. kernel-like source), and record the file count.
Pick patterns: a \b word pattern, a look-around pattern (?<=x)y and (?=...), a plain literal with an inner literal, and a no-match literal for traversal-only timing.
Time 5 runs each of 13.0.0 and 14.0.0 per pattern and per corpus, using wall-clock medians. Check run-to-run spread (IQR).
Check output set-equality with --sort path (and without sort for set comparison) between the two binaries for all patterns.

Isolate the traversal gain: time the no-match literal and file listing only; compare to the \b gain. If most of the \b gain disappears when regex-engine code is excluded, note that the reference is not agent-reachable.
Confirm the Debian image has no system rg binary that the agent could copy.

v1.summary: The ripgrep 13.0.0 to 14.0.0 idea is real and licensed (Unlicense OR MIT), with confirmed PR-numbered levers, but the 14.0.0 reference speedup is unpublished and the \b gain appears to depend on the regex-engine rewrite that the agent cannot vendor. Validation passes with caveats (Ref 3, Band 3, E0, lookup partial); the spike must measure how much gain comes from traversal and prefilter alone before the reference S is trusted.
